display.purpose: Every heading tag (h1-h6), both tiers, always tracking-tight.

body.purpose: Body copy, UI chrome, form labels.

shadows.name: ambient-card
shadows.purpose: Storefront glass-panel resting shadow. Not used on admin/POS.

shadows.name: glow-hover
shadows.purpose: Storefront glass-panel-hover escalation, Signal-Red-tinted. Storefront only.

components.name: Glass Card (Storefront)
components.description: Premium-tier card shell: translucent, blurred, soft ambient shadow. Escalates on hover with a Signal-Red-tinted glow.
components.css: .ds-card-glass { background: rgba(15,23,42,0.02); backdrop-filter: blur(16px); -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(16px); border: 1px solid rgba(15,23,42,0.05); box-shadow: 0 4px 6px -1px rgba(0,0,0,0.05), 0 2px 4px -1px rgba(0,0,0,0.03); border-radius: 12px; padding: 24px; transition: all 0.3s cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-card-glass:hover { background: rgba(15,23,42,0.04); border-color: rgba(220,38,38,0.25); box-shadow: 0 10px 30px -10px rgba(220,38,38,0.1); transform: translateY(-2px); }

components.name: Flat Card (Admin/POS)
components.description: Minimalist-tier card: same shell primitive, no shadow, no hover escalation. Depth via hairline border only.
components.css: .ds-card-flat { background: hsl(0 0% 100%); border: 1px solid hsl(214.3 31.8% 91.4%); border-radius: 12px; padding: 20px; }

components.name: Focus Ring (Signal)
components.description: Colored focus-within glow for form fields — Signal Red or Fleet Navy variant depending on context.
components.css: .ds-input-glow-red { border: 1px solid hsl(214.3 31.8% 91.4%); border-radius: 10px; padding: 10px 14px; transition: border-color 0.2s, box-shadow 0.2s; } .ds-input-glow-red:focus-within { border-color: rgba(220,38,38,0.5); box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px rgba(220,38,38,0.15); outline: none; }

narrative.overview: Everything this system does is a fitment problem solved twice over: parts have to fit the truck, and the interface has to fit whoever's using it. One visual identity, expressed at two different volumes rather than two different brands. Fleet Navy and Signal Red run through both tiers; the storefront turns the volume up (glass-panel depth, soft motion), admin/POS turns the same materials down (flat, quiet, fast).
keyCharacteristics: Fitment is the story, not an afterthought.
One palette, two intensities: Persuade-mode storefront vs Operate-mode admin/POS.
Glass-panel is the shared card primitive; its hover-glow escalation is a storefront-only privilege.
Signal Red is reserved for real signal — not decoration.

rules.name: The Two-Red Rule
rules.body: Signal Red (hover/attention) and Alarm Red (destructive/error) are never interchangeable. If it can be undone with an undo toast, it's Signal. If it just deleted something, it's Alarm.

rules.name: The Display-Everywhere Rule
rules.body: Every h1-h6, in both tiers, renders in Cabinet Grotesk with tightened tracking. The tiers differ in motion and depth, not typeface.

rules.name: The Flat-Admin Rule
rules.body: glass-panel is a shared primitive both tiers may use for the card shell, but glass-panel-hover's glow/lift escalation is a storefront-only privilege. Admin/POS stops at the flat shell.

dos: Do treat Signal Red and Alarm Red as different tokens with different meanings.
Do keep font-display on every heading in both tiers.
Do break card-grid symmetry on the storefront (bento/zig-zag over three-equal-column rows).
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion on every custom keyframe.
donts: Don't add glass-panel-hover's glow/lift escalation to an admin/POS surface.
Don't introduce a second gray/border color alongside hairline.
Don't let the storefront read as a stock e-commerce template or the admin read as a generic dashboard-by-numbers.
Don't invent a Button component's visual spec from scratch mid-task; none exists yet.
